label: History
value: The aim of Mombi and the Wizard of Oz was to keep Princess Ozma hidden
unit: Years before the events of the series, Mombi conspired with the Wizard of Oz to keep the realm's true ruler, Princess Ozma, hidden. Mombi transformed the baby princess into a young boy named Tip and raised him harshly in the Gillikin Country. When Tip attempted to scare her with a wooden jack-lantern named Jack Pumpkinhead, Mombi brought Jack to life using the Powder of Life she bought from Dr. Pipt. Threatening to turn Tip into a marble statue, Mombi prompted Tip to flee with Jack, eventually leading to General Jinjur's revolt against the Scarecrow. Mombi allied with General Jinjur to help maintain control of the Emerald City using her magic. When Glinda the Good arrived to restore the rightful ruler of Oz, Mombi attempted to escape by shape-shifting into various animals, including a rose, a griffin, and a stream of water. Glinda captured her and forced her to reveal the truth about Tip's identity. Glinda then removed Mombi's magical powers and turned her into a stone statue to ensure she could never cause harm again.

label: History
value: He ruled through illusions.
unit: After arriving in Oz by runaway balloon, the Wizard unified the central region and built the Emerald City, forcing the populace to wear green-tinted glasses. Fearing the Wicked Witches of the East and West, he hid in his palace and ruled through illusions and ventriloquism. When Dorothy Gale arrived seeking a way home, he demanded she destroy the Wicked Witch of the West before he would help her. Dorothy's dog Toto eventually knocked over a screen in his throne room, revealing him as a humbug. After granting symbolic gifts to the Scarecrow, Tin Woodman, and Cowardly Lion, he attempted to return to Kansas with Dorothy in a hot-air balloon, but accidentally left without her. He returned to circus life in America until an earthquake swallowed his balloon in California, sending him down into the subterranean realm of the Mangaboos where he reencountered Dorothy. He helped Dorothy, Zeb, and Jim the horse navigate dangerous underground kingdoms, including the valley of Voe and the Den of the Dragonettes. Upon reaching the surface in Oz, Princess Ozma welcomed him back, inviting him to stay permanently in the Emerald City to learn real magic.

label: History
value: Ozma reclaimed the Royal Family of Ev.
unit: Before the events of his grand conflict with Oz, the Nome King struck a bargain with the wicked King of Ev, buying the Queen of Ev and her ten children and transforming them into decorative ornaments in his palace. When Princess Ozma, Dorothy Gale, and their companions traveled to the Nome Kingdom to rescue the Ev royal family, Roquat tricked them into a guessing game that transformed most of the rescue party into knick-knacks as well. Billina the hen discovered the secret to the transformations and also exposed Roquat's ultimate vulnerability to eggs. Terrified by Billina dropping eggs, the Nome King was defeated, and Ozma reclaimed the Royal Family of Ev along with Roquat's powerful Magic Belt. Deprived of his magic belt and thoroughly humiliated, the Nome King harbors a deep hatred for Ozma and Dorothy and plots vengeance to reclaim his stolen power.

label: Personality
value: Braided Man exhibits a simple nature.
unit: He is eccentric, talkative, and extremely proud of his unique inventory of rustproof brass safety pins. Living in complete isolation, he is eager for company and delights in giving away his pins to travelers as useful gifts. He exhibits a simple, harmless nature and takes great pleasure in explaining his unusual lifestyle.

label: Personality
value: Jack is well-meaning.
unit: Jack is extremely gentle, polite, and well-meaning, though simple-minded and naive about the ways of the world. He takes life literally and often misinterprets common idioms or situations. Despite his intellectual limitations, he is loyal to his friends and possesses a cheerful, optimistic outlook. He accepts his physical fragility and the perishable nature of his pumpkin head with calm resignation.

label: History
value: The Saw-Horse accompanied the Wizard of Oz in later adventures.
unit: The Saw-Horse was created by Tip in the Gillikin Country as a makeshift horse and brought to life using Mombi's magic Powder of Life. He carried Tip and Jack Pumpkinhead on their journey toward the Emerald City, though his ears were initially lost in an accident. During the rebellion of General Jinjur, he helped Tip and his companions escape by being bound together with other materials to form the Gump, though he later returned to his individual wooden form. Glinda the Good Sorceress rewarded his loyalty by fitting his wooden legs with plates of solid gold to keep them from wearing away. Following Princess Ozma's restoration to the throne of Oz, the Saw-Horse became an official royal steed. In later adventures, he accompanied Dorothy Gale, Zeb, the Wizard of Oz, and their friends through the underground realms back to the Emerald City.

value: Immortals of the World — Member

label: Appearance
value: The rich jewels are mined from the Nome King's subterranean domain.
unit: The Nome King is a short, fat, and fierce-looking underground monarch with a long, white beard that reaches almost to his feet. He wears ornate robes and a crown adorned with rich jewels mined from his subterranean domain. His face is often red with anger or cunning triumph.

label: Personality
value: The Woggle-Bug often adopts a pompous demeanor
unit: The Woggle-Bug is intensely proud of his high level of education and intellect, often adopting a pompous and self-important demeanor. He has a passion for terrible puns and wordplay, which he presents with great seriousness to the annoyance of his companions. Despite his vanity, he is kind-hearted, loyal to his friends, and deeply dedicated to the pursuit and sharing of knowledge.

label: History
value: they are welcomed by Princess Ozma at the Emerald City
unit: Zeb meets Dorothy Gale at Hugson's Siding in California to drive her to Uncle Hugson's ranch. While on the road, a massive earthquake opens a deep fissure in the earth, causing Zeb, Dorothy, her kitten Eureka, and the horse Jim to plunge down into the subterranean realms. They land in the Land of the Mangaboos, where they meet the Wizard of Oz, who fell in his own hot-air balloon. Zeb travels with the group through various dangerous underground realms, including the Valley of Voe, the realm of the Gargoyles, and the Den of the Dragonettes. Throughout the journey, Zeb helps defend the party against strange creatures, often using his pocketknife or fists, and later a sword. After escaping the underground caverns, they arrive safely in the Land of Oz, where they are welcomed by Princess Ozma at the Emerald City. After enjoying the wonders and festivities of Oz, Zeb expresses a desire to return to his home in California, and Ozma uses her Magic Belt to send Zeb, Jim, and Eureka back to Hugson's Ranch.

label: History
value: Jim accompanies the group through the Valley of Voe.
unit: Jim is pulling a cab driven by Zeb Hugson when an earthquake opens a massive fissure in the earth, swallowing Jim, Zeb, Dorothy Gale, and Eureka into the subterranean Land of the Mangaboos. Upon arriving underground, Jim discovers that he can speak, a trait shared by all animals in fairylands. He accompanies the group through various underground realms, including the Valley of Voe and the country of the Gargoyles, often defending his companions by kicking dangerous subterranean creatures. Upon reaching the Land of Oz through the assistance of the Wizard, Jim participates in a race against the Sawhorse to prove his speed, though he is ultimately defeated. Recognizing that he is too old for work, Princess Ozma places Jim in a comfortable paddock in the Emerald City where he can live out his days in leisure.

label: Personality
value: Santa Claus lives to bring happiness to children all over the world.
unit: Santa Claus is immensely benevolent, cheerful, and generous. He lives to bring joy and happiness to children all over the world. He maintains a warm friendship with other magical beings, including Princess Ozma and the immortals of the world.

label: History
value: Langwidere is uninterested in ruling.
unit: Princess Langwidere inherited governance of the Land of Ev after her uncle, King Evoldo, enslaved his wife and ten children to the Nome King and ended his own life. Uninterested in ruling, Langwidere spent her time changing her heads and admiring her wardrobe in her palace at Evna. When Dorothy Gale, Billina, TikTok, and the Hungry Tiger arrived at her palace, Langwidere admired Dorothy's head and demanded to add it to her collection in exchange for one of her spare heads. After Dorothy refused, Langwidere angrily locked Dorothy in a high tower. Princess Ozma soon arrived with an army from Oz to rescue the royal family of Ev. Langwidere yielded to Ozma's authority, released Dorothy, and allowed Ozma's expedition to proceed to the Nome King's underground realm.

label: History
value: Glinda investigates the lineage of the rulers of Oz.
unit: Glinda first appears when Dorothy Gale and her companions travel south to her ruby palace seeking a way for Dorothy to return to Kansas. Glinda graciously reveals that Dorothy's Silver Shoes had the power to take her home all along, and she uses the Golden Cap's remaining wishes to send the Scarecrow, Tin Woodman, and Cowardly Lion back to their respective domains before releasing the Winged Monkeys. Later, Tip and his companions travel to Glinda's castle to seek her assistance against General Jinjur's army. Glinda investigates the lineage of the rulers of Oz and discovers that Princess Ozma, the rightful heir, was hidden away by the Wizard; she forces the witch Mombi to restore Ozma to her true form and establishes her on the throne of the Emerald City. Subsequently, Glinda remains the most powerful magical guardian of Oz, consulted during national affairs and crises.

label: Personality
value: Dorothy is kind-hearted.
unit: Dorothy is brave, kind-hearted, loyal, and level-headed. She possesses a natural practical sense that helps her handle strange and dangerous situations with calm determination. She forms quick friendships with the unusual creatures she meets and constantly seeks to help others in distress. Despite the wonders she witnesses, she deeply values her home and family above all else.

label: History
value: After Glinda restored Princess Ozma to the throne of Oz, the Woggle-Bug was appointed to found the Royal College of Art and Athletics in the Emerald City.
unit: The Woggle-Bug spent his early life crawling about a country schoolhouse, absorbing all the geography, history, and science taught by the schoolmaster, Professor Nowitall. One day, the schoolmaster caught him and placed him in a magic lantern to project his enlarged image onto a screen. Taking advantage of his new giant size, the Woggle-Bug escaped through a window to seek his fortune in Oz. He encountered Tip, Jack Pumpkinhead, the Sawhorse, and the Scarecrow, joining their party as they fled General Jinjur's Army of Revolt. After Glinda restored Princess Ozma to the throne of Oz, the Woggle-Bug was appointed to found and manage the Royal College of Art and Athletics in the Emerald City. In subsequent years, he remained a respected scholar in Oz, known for his eccentric lectures, grand fashion sense, and fondness for puns.

label: Personality
value: The Scarecrow approaches dangers with optimism.
unit: Despite initially believing he lacked brains, the Scarecrow is exceptionally clever, insightful, and resourceful. He is gentle, loyal, and good-natured, always willing to sacrifice his own safety to help his friends. He takes great pride in the 'brains' given to him by the Wizard, though he possessed natural wisdom all along. He approaches dangers with calm logic and optimism.

label: Titles
value: Wicked Witch of the West

label: Appearance
value: Zeb Hugson wears typical country clothing.
unit: Zeb Hugson is a young American farm boy who wears typical country clothing suitable for working on a California ranch. He is slender and youthful, often seen driving his horse and buggy. During his adventures underground, he carries his pocketknife and travels alongside his old farm horse, Jim.

label: History
value: The Tin Woodman was oiled by Dorothy Gale
unit: After being oiled and freed by Dorothy Gale and the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman joined their journey to the Emerald City to ask the Wizard of Oz for a heart. Along the way, he helped defeat numerous threats using his axe and befriended the Cowardly Lion. Sent by the Wizard to destroy the Wicked Witch of the West, he was dismantled by the Witch's Winkie slaves, but his tin body was later repaired by the Winkies after her defeat. In gratitude for liberating them, the Winkies invited him to become their ruler, a title he accepted as Emperor after receiving a silk-and-sawdust heart from the Wizard. Later, he accompanied Dorothy on her quest to find Glinda the Good Witch and helped defend the group against various monsters. When Dorothy returned to Oz via the earthquake, he reunited with her at the Emerald City, participated in the Wizard's trial, and helped celebrate Ozma's court before returning to his domain.

label: History
value: The reason Eureka gains the ability to speak is due to fairy realm magic.
unit: Eureka is introduced when a massive earthquake in California swallows Dorothy, Zeb, Jim the Horse, and Eureka in her basket, dropping them into the subterranean realm of Mangaboo. Throughout their journey through various underground kingdoms, Eureka gains the ability to speak due to fairy realm magic. She frequently gets into arguments with Jim the Horse and the Nine Tiny Piglets, whom she views as potential prey. Upon reaching the Land of Oz, Eureka becomes embroiled in a serious incident when one of the Wizard's Nine Tiny Piglets vanishes, and she is accused of eating it. A formal trial is held in the Emerald City, where Eureka refuses to clear her name out of pride and spite, coming close to being executed. However, the missing piglet is eventually found alive after having been hidden away by Eureka as a joke, proving her innocence of murder though revealing her deceitful prank. Following the trial, Princess Ozma uses the Magic Belt to send Eureka back to her home in Kansas.

label: History
value: Following her death, the Winkies were freed from her tyranny.
unit: The Wicked Witch of the West ruled the Winkie Country in the western quarter of Oz, enslaving the native Winkies. When Dorothy Gale and her companions were sent by the Wizard of Oz to destroy her, the Witch spotted them with her single eye. She sent wolves, crows, and bees to destroy them, but Dorothy's companions repelled each assault. She then used the magical Golden Cap for the third and final time to command the Winged Monkeys, who destroyed the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman, captured the Cowardly Lion, and brought Dorothy to her castle. The Witch forced Dorothy to work as a servant and tried to starve the Lion into submission. Spotting the magical Silver Shoes on Dorothy's feet, the Witch tricked Dorothy into tripping so she could steal one shoe. Enraged, Dorothy threw a bucket of water over the Witch, causing her to melt completely into a brown, shapeless mass. Following her death, the Winkies were freed from her tyranny and appointed the Tin Woodman as their new ruler.

label: History
value: The Cowardly Lion hopes that the Wizard will grant him courage.
unit: The Cowardly Lion first meets Dorothy, the Scarecrow, and the Tin Woodman in the yellow brick road's forest, joining their quest to Emerald City in hopes that the Wizard will grant him courage. During the journey, he leaps across perilous chasms, fights off the Kalidahs, and carries his friends to safety. When sent to defeat the Wicked Witch of the West, he is captured and imprisoned, but he refuses to work for her until Dorothy frees him after destroying the witch. Upon returning to the Wizard, the Lion drinks a potion presented as courage, which restores his confidence. On the journey south to see Glinda, he slays a giant spider-like monster terrorizing an ancient forest, earning the title of King of Beasts from its animal inhabitants. He later joins Ozma's birthday celebrations and aids Dorothy and Princess Ozma in their adventures, including descending into the underground realms to rescue companions after the earthquake in California.

label: Appearance
value: Uncle Henry looks gray.
unit: Uncle Henry is an elderly farmer who looks worn and gray from years of hard labor in the harsh Kansas environment. He has a solemn countenance that rarely cracks into a smile, reflecting the stern reality of his impoverished life on the prairie.

label: History
value: During her brief reign, Jinjur forces the men of the city to perform domestic chores.
unit: Jinjur first appears in the second Oz book, where she recruits and leads an Army of Revolt made up of young maidens who wish to take over the Emerald City and gain control of its jewels and wealth. Taking advantage of the city's undefended state while the Scarecrow is absent, Jinjur successfully besieges the capital, drives out the Scarecrow upon his return, and declares herself Queen of Oz. During her brief reign, she forces the men of the city to perform domestic chores while her soldiers feast on royal sweets and wear fine jewels. Her rule is challenged when Tip, the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, and their companions attempt to reclaim the throne, though she temporarily repels them using her cunning and guard force. Ultimately, Glinda the Good Witch marches on the Emerald City with her own army, easily surrounding Jinjur's forces. Realizing resistance is futile and terrified of Glinda's soldiers, Jinjur surrenders the city. After Princess Ozma is restored as the rightful ruler, Jinjur is pardoned and returns to her home, eventually settling down to a quiet life of domesticity.

label: Appearance
value: Santa Claus has a white beard.
unit: Santa Claus is an elderly man with a jolly face, a white beard, and a hearty demeanor. He is traditionally dressed in warm, bright clothing suited for his travels. He travels in a sleigh pulled by magical reindeer.

label: Appearance
value: Tiktok is round.
unit: Tiktok is a round, copper clockwork man with polished joints and a cheerful metallic face. He has three separate clockwork mechanisms inside him that control his thinking, speaking, and action. Each mechanism must be wound up independently using a key. When his machinery runs down, he stops moving or speaking entirely until wound up again.

label: Personality
value: Ozma is kind-hearted.
unit: Ozma is wise, kind-hearted, and compassionate toward all the inhabitants of Oz and her friends. She is a dignified ruler who prefers justice, peace, and gentleness over harsh punishment. Despite her royal status, she remains accessible, friendly, and deeply loyal to those who assist her.
